subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a static truck prop, designing it as rigid geometry without joints, roughly 7m long, 2.8m wide, and 3m tall, facing the +Z direction.

Working out helper functions for boxes and glowing parts, plus textured plane details like hazard stripes and a cyberpunk sign. I'm positioning six wheels across three axles and laying out the chassis dimensions and wheel arch placement along the z-axis.

Now I'm figuring out the fenders above the wheels and shaping the cab using an extruded side profile with a sloped windshield outline.

For texture, I'm leaning toward a military armored look with a panelled mottled olive/dark-slate color scheme including subtle rivets, applying it as the hull's paint material.

I'm redefining the cab profile with a sloped windshield segment and placing a thin angled slab to represent the glass between the hood corner and roofline.

Working out the rotation angle for the windshield box so its face aligns with the slope's normal direction...

That gives roughly -40.6°, so I offset the windshield outward along the normal and give it a dark tinted cyan glow with wiper details. Next I'm positioning side window panels on the cab's flat sides, sizing them against the roof height and slope transition point.

Now I'm placing the headlights, light bar, front bumper with hazard stripes, and grille boxes at the front face, then moving to the rear bed platform and mounting an armored cargo container behind the cab.

For the rooftop missile launcher, I'm planning a tilted pod rack with a 2x4 grid of tubes angled upward and forward, computing each tube's position by rotating local offsets with a quaternion and building each tube as a rod from base point to aimed endpoint.

Still shaping the pod box...

Now I'm planning a turret for the cab roof, centered above the cab with a base cylinder, boxy head, twin barrels with muzzle brakes, an ammo box, and a sensor camera with a glowing red eye.

For the container I'm sizing it roughly 2.3x1.1x3.0, positioned behind the cab, then working out clearance for a launcher pod on the deck so it doesn't collide with the container or cab — adjusting the pod's z-position and support pivot to fit the gap.

Now I'm thinking through the surface details: hazard stripes, rear door seams, vents, glowing edge strips, roof antennas, a sensor dish, cable runs, and hex-plated panels for a drone launch pad on top of the container.

Adding the side armor skirts, cylindrical fuel tanks, and dual exhaust stacks with glowing orange heat rings behind the cab. For the wheels I'm weighing whether to build full tread-block geometry per tire or keep it simpler to stay within part budget.

Still building wheel geometry...

Now I'm adding fender plates and raised mudguards over the wheels, then working out the underbody with axle cylinders, drive shaft, chassis rails, and the hull box dimensions for ground clearance.

Moving to cab details next: roof light bar, vents, mirrors, door seams and handles, armor plates, grille with glow slits, and dual headlights, plus rear tail lights and bumper on the container.

For textures I'm planning around six: hazard stripes, a cyberpunk emblem decal for the door, window texture, a neon HUD/sign panel with text like "NOVA-77 / ARES", a stenciled number decal, and maybe a hologram sign — skipping grille and camo textures as unnecessary. I'm thinking decals will be implemented as textured plane parts oriented to face outward from the hull.

I'm confirming no mirroring issues since each plane faces outward toward the viewer with standard up orientation, and that glow works fine on textured parts as long as they use flat colors and a single standard material, keeping the overall color palette small.

Now I'm writing helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and glow application, then setting up mirrored symmetry loops and starting to lay out the color palette for the design.

Defining palette colors...

Adding more container details...

Now I'm figuring out fuel tank placement between the axles, positioning cylinders at the sides with rotation so they lie horizontally, checking clearance against the front and rear wheels, and adding thin cylinder bands as decorative rings around each tank. Next I'm considering skirt armor over the rear dual wheels.

I decide to skip the skirt and instead add fender flares and glowing mud flaps behind the wheels, then design the front bull bar bumper with a hazard-striped plane and a row of angled spike cones for a wedge-plow look, plus a winch cylinder with a red cable mounted at the front. Finally I'm sketching the turret assembly, stacking a base cylinder on the roof armor with a head box on top to form the turret structure.

I'm adding twin gun barrels extending forward from the turret head with muzzle brake cylinders, flanking ammo boxes, and a sensor pod with a glowing red eye sphere, checking that the barrels clear the windshield slope. I'm also positioning a roof lightbar on the sloped section of the roof with alternating cyan and magenta glow to avoid colliding with the turret head.

Now I'm placing exhaust stacks at the cab's rear corners behind the cab, sizing cylinders with glowing orange top caps and adding heat shields and clamp rings, then adding cyan underglow boxes beneath the hull sides.

Adding front corner armor skirts, mirror arms and mirror boxes on each side, door seam details with vertical and horizontal trim lines, door emblem decals, cab-side steps, and planning the rear container door with hazard stripe texturing.

I'm sketching the rear details: door seams, red tail lights, and a license plate reading "2077" along with a rear hitch, then deciding to skip roof hex panels. I'm also considering a drone landing pad on the container roof with an upward-facing glow ring, oriented to point straight up.

Writing SVG texture code...

For the emblem I'm designing a hexagonal shield with cyan stroke, magenta inner chevrons, and stylized "7" bolt text on a transparent background, and for the container side sign I'm laying out a dark rectangle with neon "ARES-77" and "ORBITAL DEFENSE" text, skipping kanji in favor of Latin characters.

I'm also planning a glowing glass window with diagonal reflection streaks and HUD lines, a license plate reading "2077 N-CAL", a landing pad with an H ring marker, a radar screen with sweeping green blips, and a glowing red turret camera eye. With around 250 parts estimated total, I'm noting the part-creation API signature (geometry, color, placement options including rotation in degrees) so I can write the generation code efficiently.

Now I'm working out the wheel geometry function -- positioning the tire cylinder, adding tread blocks arranged radially around it using trigonometry for angle-based placement, and alternating their offsets to create a realistic tread pattern.

I'm adding the rim cylinder, lug nuts, and a neon torus accent on the outer face, while making sure the rotation math keeps everything symmetric and only the visible outer side needs full detail.

Now I'm wiring up the axles and thinking about reusing a coil component from the clockwork kit for the suspension springs...

Writing shock absorber geometry...

Now I'm adding random greebles like vents and crates to the roof using a seeded RNG for deterministic placement, then setting up color constants and point helper functions for the windshield slope, working out the tangent and outward normal for the angled glass panel.

Computing the windshield box rotation...

I'll skip the frame and apply the window texture directly onto boxes for the windshield and side windows, using a 100x50 viewBox texture at matching aspect ratios.

Now I'm planning the remaining details: side armor plates with bolt rows along the sides, draping a cable sweep from cab to container pod, and sorting out TypeScript typing for coordinate arrays before writing the final code.

Then I'm working out positions for the bumper, headlights, grille, and light bar on the cab's front face, using the bumper box depth to figure out where each plane should sit relative to the cab's front z-coordinate.

I'll skip the winch cable detail for now and focus on finishing the write-up around 500 lines.
